claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has excellent high-temperature mechanical performance.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility.
The irradiation tolerance of NbMoTaW has been inferred computationally but not confirmed experimentally.
The proposed intervention is to substitute 2–5 atomic percent vanadium for an unspecified constituent of NbMoTaW.
Adding 2–5 atomic percent vanadium will preserve a BCC matrix in NbMoTaW.
Vanadium incorporation will subtly modify the BCC lattice.
The vanadium-induced lattice modifications will enhance dislocation mobility.
The vanadium-induced lattice modifications will accelerate recombination of irradiation-induced defects.
Vanadium addition will reduce barriers to dislocation motion at room temperature.
Vanadium has sufficiently high solubility and diffusivity in the proposed alloy to promote irradiation-defect recombination.
Reduced barriers to dislocation motion will increase room-temperature ductility relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Enhanced defect recombination will reduce irradiation-induced void swelling relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Vanadium alloying will reduce helium-induced blistering relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
The vanadium-modified alloy will have higher room-temperature elongation to failure than untreated NbMoTaW.
The vanadium-modified alloy will maintain mechanical performance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW at temperatures up to approximately 1600 °C.
The proposed benefits apply from room temperature to approximately 1600 °C.
The proposed irradiation benefit applies under conditions typical of helium-ion implantation experiments.
